outcome_verbatim: Employment status was derived from the Employment Classification Module (AKM), where based on the main source of income or employment, annual status of most important employment is classified. Individuals who were unemployed, retired (including early retirement and disability pension), and otherwise not working were categorized as outside the labour market. | Results, Employment: 'In absolute proportions, at the age of 25, 87% of the individuals with schizophrenia were not employed, and at the age of 60, 85% of the individuals with schizophrenia were not employed.'
source_locator: Results, Employment, p. 1346 (text); the same series appears only as an unlabelled line in Fig. 1, right panel, p. 1345. Diagnosis-group size at Results, Sample, p. 1346. Outcome definition at Materials and methods, Labour market and social exclusion outcomes, p. 1344
notes: NUMERATOR DELIBERATELY BLANK. The only absolute employment figures in the article are whole-number percentages in the text (87% not employed at age 25) and an unlabelled line graph (Fig. 1, right panel). No denominator appears anywhere in the held PDF, and the Online Appendix Tables 1-3 cited in the Results are NOT in it, so even the manifest's 9,444 could not be seen. Multiplying a whole-number percentage by a denominator is forbidden by codebook rule 2 however exact the denominator looks: at 87% on about 9,444 the rounding interval alone spans roughly plus or minus 47 while the binomial standard error is about 33, so the reconstruction error would exceed the sampling error it replaces. Taking the complement of a rounded percentage is the same operation and is equally forbidden. THE CONSTRUCT IS NOT paid_any. AKM classifies the single most important employment status of the year from the main source of income, so a person whose main income is a disability pension is 'outside the labour market' even if they did some paid work. That is a dominance criterion which excludes low-intensity paid work exactly as an hours threshold would, and it must never substitute for paid_any; paid_intensity_threshold is the vocabulary value that carries the non-substitutability, and the fit is imperfect because the threshold is a dominance rule rather than a stated percentage of working days, which is raised in unresolved_queries.md U3. THE TIMEPOINT IS AN AGE, NOT AN ELAPSED FOLLOW-UP (D12.3b): schizophrenia was first diagnosed anywhere between ages 15 and 25, so elapsed time since diagnosis at age 25 ranges from zero to ten years. followup_basis = chronological_age bars this result from every landmark horizon, independently of the missing counts. NOT EXTRACTED, and noted here so the omission is visible: the same paragraph gives 85% and 56% not employed at ages 25 and 60 for the post-hoc subgroup not rehospitalised for schizophrenia after age 25 (6,328 of 9,448 were rehospitalised), which is a subgroup, not a whole cohort, and carries no counts either.

notes: TRIAGE FIGURE 968/6939 VERIFIED, and verified from two independent printed places rather than reconstructed: the numerator 968 is printed as a count in the Results, and the denominator 6,939 is printed in Table 1 at year 0 and again in the Results as the number of individuals whose first inpatient diagnosis was schizophrenia. 968/6939 = 13.95%, which rounds to the printed 14%. The other two groups reconcile identically (11,335/34,565 = 32.8% against a printed 33%; 3,875/9,047 = 42.8% against a printed 43%), and the two printed control figures reconcile too (112,259/172,825 = 65.0%; 31,242/45,235 = 69.1%), so the whole sentence is internally consistent. The denominator is a genuine observed denominator and not a reporting base: the methods state 'If an individual did not have data for a certain year, the corresponding case or control participant was not included in the statistical analyses', and Table 1 prints the resulting per-year counts. CONSTRUCT: 'working or self-employed' with no dominance, hours or earnings qualifier, so this is paid_any. Note that the OTHER Hakulinen report in this batch uses a different and narrower definition; the two must not be treated as the same measure. ASCERTAINMENT: employment status in the last week of the calendar year, a reference-week measure and therefore point prevalence, not the tax-year period prevalence registers usually give; the one-week reference period is recorded here rather than in ascertainment_window_months, which is reserved for period prevalence. TIMEPOINT: 'time point zero represented the year when the first hospitalization ... occurred for each case participant', and the measurement is at the END of that calendar year, so elapsed time from cohort entry ranges from under a week for someone hospitalised in late December to nearly twelve months for someone hospitalised in January. followup_basis = calendar_end_common records that; the vocabulary's wording says 'one shared calendar end date' whereas this is a per-participant year end, which is raised in unresolved_queries.md U5. source_locator: Table 3 'Univariate linear and logistic regressions on whether financial deprivation at baseline predicts clinical, functioning, and neurocognitive outcomes at 4 years', Functional outcomes at 4 years, row 'Unemployed, n (%)', p. 291; flow at Fig. 1, p. 285; construct at Methods, Clinical, functional, and neurocognitive outcomes, p. 286
notes: TRIAGE FIGURE 158/219 REFUTED AS A RECOVERABLE COUNT, and n_employed and n_outcome_observed are deliberately blank. What Table 3 prints at four years is 'Unemployed, n (%) 40 (65.6%) / 21 (34.4%)'. THOSE ARE ROW PERCENTAGES OF THE 61 UNEMPLOYED, NOT COLUMN PERCENTAGES: 40 + 21 = 61, 40/61 = 65.6% and 21/61 = 34.4%. Read as column percentages they would imply 65.6% of 112 = 73 unemployed in the deprived group, which is wrong. So the printed percentages carry NO information whatever about the denominator on which the employment variable was observed, which is why reported_percentage_base is 61 and n_outcome_observed is blank (prompt rule 7). No employed count is printed at four years at all; 158/219 would come from subtracting 61 from 219, and 219 would come from summing two column headers. That fails D12.2 twice over: its components would be two deprivation subgroups with different arm identities and different denominators (112 and 107), so they neither share an arm nor share one denominator. THE CANDIDATE VALUES, for an author query and NOT for use: if employment status were observed for all 112 and all 107, the complement gives 72/112 deprived and 86/107 non-deprived, totalling 158/219. Three things support that reading and one refutes it. Supporting: Fig. 1 shows 234 at baseline and '4-year follow-up analysis (n=219, 93.6%)' with 112 and 107 reconciling exactly (121-9 and 113-6); the employment variable had zero missingness at baseline (45+76 = 121 and 85+28 = 113 exactly); and the crude odds ratio those denominators imply, (40/72)/(21/86) = 2.28, is within one per cent of the printed adjusted OR of 2.29 (exp(0.83), and the geometric centre of [1.173, 4.492] is 2.295). Refuting: this paper demonstrably does not apply its column headers to every variable, since Table 1 reports t(213) and t(215) and Table 4 reports t(206) to t(208) against a stated n of 234, so per-variable denominators differ and are never printed. A denominator inferred against the paper's own evidence is not an observed denominator. See unresolved_queries.md U6. CONSTRUCT IS unclear: 'employment status (employed or not)' is never defined, so it is not established whether paid sheltered work, part-time work or student status were counted, and coding it paid_any would substitute an undefined measure for the primary construct. POPULATION: 120 of the 360 randomised were excluded from the analysis 'to better isolate the impact of financial deprivation on psychosis recovery outcomes', so the 240 is two of three allocation groups and not a whole recruited cohort; the row can never enter the prevalence intercept whatever the counts. Denominators recorded: n_entered 240 (entering the deprivation classification), n_alive_eligible 228 (234 with income data less the 6 deceased), n_assessed 219 (the 4-year follow-up analysis sample). MODERATORS: mean_age 37.9 is the n-weighted mean of the two printed group means (38.65 on 121 and 37.13 on 113), which is exact arithmetic on printed values rather than a back-calculation; n_female 128 = 70 + 58 and n_employed_baseline 130 = 45 + 85, each on the printed 234.

notes: TRIAGE FIGURE 36/46 VERIFIED: printed as a count over its denominator in Results 3.2, and 36/46 = 78.26% matches the printed 78.3%. THIS IS NOT paid_any AND MUST NOT SUBSTITUTE FOR IT.
